text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The opposition Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) have denied they had agreed to merge after secret talks.
- A cabinet directive to retire civil servants at the age of 55 has affected rural health centres and some of them face imminent closure due to lack of staff, the health ministry said.
- The Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) chairman, Chipimpha Mughogho, said his party had no plans to join the main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP).
- Up to 21 people have died as a result of heavy rain over the past two months, a police official said.
- Police raided the office of former president Kamuzu Banda's Press Corporation in Lilongwe and a high shool owned by him to search for documents.

- Shadow education minister for the Malawi Congress Party (MCP), Kate Kainja, has slammed Malawi's education minister for tranforming some distance education learning centres into secondary schools after first promising to build 250 secondary schools.
